## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Rai Way is not a growth story and has never pretended to be one. The core narrative across the available window is a **regulated-utility-like broadcast-tower annuity** (≈65-66% EBITDA margins, single-digit revenue growth indexed loosely to inflation, low leverage, high dividend payout) onto which a **single transformational M&A catalyst** — the long-rumoured combination with EI Towers (Italy's other national broadcast-tower operator, owned by F2i and MFE/MediaForEurope) to create a ~€4bn national tower champion — has been bolted.

- **Capex mix shift to solar/self-generation** is a quiet hedge against the one cost line (electricity) that swings EBITDA — a smart, under-discussed defensive move that modestly de-risks the annuity regardless of the deal.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: STABLE (with a PERPETUALLY-PENDING catalyst overlay).** The underlying business is a stable, high-FCF, deleveraging broadcast-tower annuity trading at a structurally unjustified ~28% EV/EBITDA discount to its closest Italian peer. That alone is a defensible, paid-to-wait value position. Bolted on top is a transformational EI Towers merger that would crystallise synergies and a €310–400M special dividend — but which is **non-binding, has missed two prior deadlines, is controlled by RAI/F2i/MFE and the Italian government, gates on a Mediaset contract negotiation RAI Way isn't party to, and has regressed to arguing 'governance principles' 18 months in.**

**The single most important thing to weigh before sizing:** *do not size this as a dated, binding merger-arb.* Size it as a **cheap, high-yielding defensive infrastructure annuity with a free, long-dated merger/special-dividend call option.** The annuity + the 28% peer discount justify a position on their own; the catalyst justifies *patience and a modest option-value premium*, not conviction-level sizing or a clock-driven entry. The 15-Jun-2026 date is far likelier to produce another extension than a signed deal — underwrite to the standalone value (~€6–6.5 on a re-rate toward peers) and treat any binding announcement or special-dividend declaration as upside, not the base case.

bull_thesis:
Rai Way owns the physical network that carries Italy's public television and radio signals - roughly 2,300 towers and transmission sites plus the satellite, microwave and fibre links between them. It cannot be rebuilt. The planning permissions and emissions consents attached to those sites are effectively unobtainable today, and the national coverage obligation that pays for the network is a legal public-service mandate rather than a commercial choice. That is a genuine, permissioned, physical moat, and it shows up in the returns: 25.3% on invested capital and 47.0% on equity over the twelve months to June 2026, with cash profit margins of 64.9%. Most listed companies never touch those numbers.

The bull case is that the market has repriced the multiple on this asset without the earnings power having changed. The shares trade at EUR 4.57 in Milan against a twelve-month high of EUR 6.34 - down about 28% - and sit roughly 17% below their 200-day average, only 4% up off the low. Yet revenue has never fallen in eleven years as a listed company: EUR 230 million in 2021, EUR 283 million in 2025, EUR 286.6 million over the twelve months to June 2026. Operating cash flow was EUR 141.8 million in 2025 against a market value today of about EUR 1.23 billion. Free cash flow runs at roughly EUR 107 to EUR 124 million a year depending on whether you charge the full property and equipment spend or the narrower capital-expenditure line, which is a free cash flow yield somewhere between 8.6% and 10.1%. The dividend, most recently EUR 0.33 a share, yields about 7.2% and is covered by that cash flow.

Three specific things support a re-rating. First, management raised full-year guidance on 30 July 2026 on the back of first-half results, and delivered the first quarter exactly as advertised - core revenue up 2.6% to EUR 71.9 million, matching the guided number to the decimal. Second, the analyst community models an acceleration, not a decline: consensus revenue of EUR 290.3 million in 2026, EUR 303.9 million in 2027, EUR 315.4 million in 2028 and EUR 360 million by 2030, with earnings per share reaching EUR 0.406. That is compound revenue growth of about 4.4% a year. Nobody serious is forecasting terminal decline in this business. Third, the balance sheet is not a constraint: net debt of EUR 168.0 million at 30 June 2026, including EUR 26.7 million of capitalised leases, is only 0.90 times cash profit, and the Altman solvency score of 3.9 is comfortably out of the danger zone.

The conditions this case depends on are specific and testable. The anchor contract with RAI, the state broadcaster that also owns about two-thirds of the company, must be renewed on economics that resemble today's. The reset of the 2027 outlook that appears to have driven the sharpest leg of the de-rating must prove to have been a timing revision rather than a structural downgrade. And the capital now being invested - visible in depreciation rising from EUR 47.3 million in 2023 to EUR 56.4 million in 2025 - must start producing the revenue that consensus expects from 2027 onward. If all three hold, an asset earning 25% on capital with a 7% yield and contracted revenue should not trade at 7.5 times cash profit.
bear_thesis:
The bear case is not that Rai Way is a bad business. It is that the market has already worked out what this business is actually worth to a minority shareholder, and the answer is a lot less than the returns headline suggests.

Start with the arithmetic nobody disputes. Revenue rose about 4% over the two years to June 2026. Over the same stretch operating profit fell: EUR 132.2 million in 2024, EUR 130.1 million in 2025, EUR 125.5 million over the trailing twelve months. Cash profit margin went 66.4%, 65.6%, 64.9%. Operating margin went 47.9%, 45.7%, 43.8% - about 400 basis points of compression in two years. Net margin went 32.6%, 31.4%, 29.8%. Earnings per share have printed EUR 0.32, EUR 0.33 and EUR 0.33 for three consecutive years and have now slipped to EUR 0.314 on a trailing basis, with the June 2026 quarter down about 10% year on year at EUR 0.0827 against EUR 0.092. A company whose revenue rises while every profit line falls is spending more capital to stand still, and the depreciation line confirms it - up about 19% since 2023 while cash profit went nowhere.

Second, the guidance raise on 30 July 2026 sits awkwardly against the half it was raised on. First-half 2026 revenue was EUR 144.1 million against EUR 142.3 million, up 1.3%. First-half cash profit was EUR 95.1 million against EUR 96.0 million - down 0.9%. First-half net profit was EUR 44.1 million against EUR 47.3 million - down 6.7%. Lifting a full-year outlook in a half where both profit measures declined is a tension the public record does not resolve, and the market's answer was to sell the stock anyway.

Third, and most importantly, this is one contract. RAI is both the controlling shareholder, with about two-thirds of the equity, and by a wide margin the largest customer. That is not a diversified tower company with competing tenants bidding for space; it is a cost-plus relationship negotiated with a counterparty who also controls the board. The counterparty is a state broadcaster funded by an Italian licence fee that politicians revisit regularly. When that contract is repriced, the minority shareholder is not at the table. The peer comparison that makes this stock look cheap against the European tower operators quietly assumes there is no idiosyncratic overhang; the overhang is the ownership structure itself, and it is visible in plain sight.

Fourth, the payout is now doing balance-sheet work. Dividends of EUR 89.7 million in 2025 consumed about 101% of reported net profit. Net debt moved from EUR 113.6 million at end-March 2026 to EUR 168.0 million at end-June - a EUR 54 million swing in the quarter the dividend was paid - and shareholders' equity fell from EUR 213.8 million to EUR 147.5 million over the same three months. Leverage is still low, but a dividend that exceeds earnings and is partly funded by borrowing is a dividend with a shelf life if the investment programme continues.

Fifth, the market repriced this for reasons, not out of panic. Kepler Cheuvreux, which had a Buy and a EUR 6.70 target on 11 May 2026, downgraded to Hold with a EUR 5.20 target on 9 July 2026. Morgan Stanley published Equalweight with a EUR 5.40 target on 26 August 2026. Both current targets sit below any bullish reading of fair value. And a 0.42-beta, 7%-yielding infrastructure asset is a bond substitute: with long-dated government yields at nineteen-year highs, the discount rate applied to this cash flow stream has risen mechanically, and no amount of operational delivery fixes that.

What would confirm the bear case: the 11 November 2026 third-quarter report showing the guidance raise walked back or the 2027 outlook cut again; any disclosure that the RAI contract is being renegotiated on worse terms; a fourth consecutive quarter of falling earnings per share; or a dividend rebased to restore coverage. Any one of those would take the shares below EUR 4.00 quickly, because the shareholder register here is full of people who own it for the yield and nothing else.
consensus_delta:
Where we disagree with the market is narrower than the 28% drawdown suggests, and being honest about that is the point of this section.

The street is not pricing terminal decline into this company. That is the first thing to establish, because with a stock 28% off its high and sitting 4% off a twelve-month low, the reflex is to assume the market has written the business off. It has not. Consensus models revenue rising from EUR 290.3 million in 2026 to EUR 303.9 million in 2027, EUR 315.4 million in 2028 and EUR 360 million by 2030, with earnings per share of EUR 0.406 by the end of that path - compound revenue growth of about 4.4% a year. Analysts are forecasting an acceleration from the roughly 2% the company actually delivers today. So the fashionable deep-value framing - the street thinks broadcast towers are dying, we know they are not - is simply false here. Nobody thinks they are dying.

What the market has actually done is compress the multiple while leaving the forecasts alone, and there are two identifiable reasons, one of which we think is right and one of which we think is overdone.

The reason we think is right: the anchor contract is a genuine structural discount, not a temporary fear. RAI owns about two-thirds of the equity and buys the large majority of the output. A minority holder in that structure does not own a monopoly's pricing power; they own whatever a controlling counterparty leaves on the table. The market is correct to demand a permanent discount for that, and any thesis that treats the gap to diversified tower operators as recoverable alpha is mispricing the governance.

The reason we think is overdone: the profit deterioration is being read as erosion when the evidence says dilution. Gross margin is stable at 56.7% while operating margin has fallen about 400 basis points in two years. Stable gross margin with falling operating margin means the pressure sits below the gross line - in depreciation, which rose from EUR 47.3 million in 2023 to EUR 56.4 million in 2025 - and not in pricing. Read literally, the legacy contract is not being priced down; new, lower-margin third-party activity is diluting a spectacular 65% cash-profit average. Growth dilution and competitive erosion look identical on a margin chart and are opposite in what they imply. The consensus 2027 acceleration is, in effect, the bet that the capital already spent starts paying. If it does, today's compressed operating margin is the trough, not the trend.

The specific street assumption we would challenge is the one embedded in the two current targets - EUR 5.20 from Kepler Cheuvreux on 9 July 2026 and EUR 5.40 from Morgan Stanley on 26 August 2026. Both sit below our EUR 5.55 base, and both were set by analysts who had been materially more positive within the last four months. That looks like targets marked to a falling price rather than to a changed forecast, which is the most common form of sell-side drift. But we are talking about a EUR 0.15 to EUR 0.35 disagreement on a EUR 4.57 stock. That is a difference of view, not an expectations arbitrage.

The disagreement worth naming, finally, is about the re-rating mechanism itself - and here we disagree with the bulls, not the bears. The most plausible route to EUR 5.55 for a 0.42-beta asset yielding 7.2% is a lower discount rate. That is a bet on long-dated yields falling, and in the current environment - the long end at nineteen-year highs, the September policy move already priced out without the long end rallying - a rate-rescue thesis is one we deliberately refuse to underwrite. Strip it out and the re-rating has to come from operational delivery alone, which takes longer and needs the 2027 plan to prove out.
forcing_function:
There is no single event that forces a re-rating here, and pretending otherwise would be the error this file is most exposed to.

The one hard date is the third-quarter report on 11 November 2026, confirmed independently and consistent with the 72-day countdown in our own screen. It matters not because a quarterly print re-rates anything by itself, but because it is the scheduled window in which two specific questions get answered: whether the full-year guidance raised on 30 July 2026 survives contact with a third quarter, and what management now says about 2027 after the outlook reset that appears to have caused the de-rating. A re-affirmed guidance plus a restored medium-term plan is the cheapest available proof that the profit decline of the last two years is investment-phase dilution rather than structural erosion. That is the thesis in a single print.

Beyond that, the events that would genuinely re-rate this business are all undated. A renewal or extension of the anchor contract with RAI on visible terms would remove the largest single discount in the valuation - but it is negotiated privately between a company and its controlling shareholder, and no external party can date it. A rebasing of the dividend to a level covered with room to spare would, paradoxically, be bullish for the equity even as it forces income holders out, because it would convert a stretched payout into a sustainable one. Any move by the Italian state on its stake, or any renewed industrial consolidation among Italian tower assets, would reprice the whole structure - but nothing of the kind could be verified as live as of 31 August 2026, and we do not underwrite what we cannot source.

What we explicitly refuse to count as a forcing function: falling long-dated yields. It is the most likely mechanical route to EUR 5.55 for an asset like this, and it is precisely the kind of rate-rescue thesis that the current environment punishes. If the case only works when the discount rate falls, it is not a case.

So the honest answer is that the driver is real and the date is not fixed, with 11 November 2026 as the nearest scheduled window in which the evidence arrives.
valley_of_death:
For a company generating EUR 141.8 million of operating cash flow a year with net debt at 0.90 times cash profit, there is no cash-burn hump and no maturity wall. The near-term risk here is entirely about disappointment, not solvency - but it is real, and it is concentrated in a single window.

The dated risk is the third-quarter report on 11 November 2026, about ten weeks away. Management raised full-year guidance on 30 July 2026 in a half-year where cash profit fell 0.9% and net profit fell 6.7%. That is a public commitment made on a weakening profit trend, and 11 November is when it gets tested. Two consecutive quarters of falling earnings per share are already on the record - the June 2026 quarter earned EUR 0.0827 against EUR 0.092 a year earlier, down about 10%. A third would confirm a trend rather than a wobble, and it would arrive alongside whatever management says about 2027 - the outlook that was reportedly reset and that the market has not forgiven.

The second near-term pressure is the balance sheet's own rhythm. Net debt rose from EUR 113.6 million at end-March 2026 to EUR 168.0 million at end-June, a EUR 54 million swing driven by the dividend, and shareholders' equity fell from EUR 213.8 million to EUR 147.5 million over the same three months. Dividends of EUR 89.7 million in 2025 consumed about 101% of reported net profit. None of that is dangerous at 0.90 times leverage. But if earnings per share keep sliding while investment continues at the EUR 50 million-a-year rate of 2024 and 2025, the coverage arithmetic gets uncomfortable inside twelve months, and a board facing that arithmetic rebases the payout. In a stock owned largely for its yield, that decision is worth more than the cash it saves.

The third pressure is macro and it is not going away on this horizon. This is a bond substitute - a 0.42-beta, 7.2%-yielding infrastructure asset - and long-dated government yields are at nineteen-year highs, with the long end refusing to rally even as near-term policy tightening was priced out. Every month that persists, the discount rate applied to this cash flow stream stays elevated and the multiple stays compressed regardless of what the company delivers. An investor buying today is accepting that the most natural re-rating mechanism is blocked for as long as that condition holds.

The risk that is genuinely unquantifiable from outside: any news on the anchor contract with RAI. It could arrive on any date, it would be material either way, and no external party has visibility into a negotiation conducted between a company and its own controlling shareholder.
positioning_washout:
This is a yield-owned stock, and that is the most important fact about its shareholder register.

The evidence is circumstantial but consistent. Eleven consecutive years of dividends since the November 2014 flotation. A current payout of about EUR 0.33 a share yielding roughly 7.2%. A beta of 0.42, which is what you get when the holders are income and low-volatility mandates rather than growth money. And an Italian mid-cap infrastructure name of this size is a natural constituent of European high-dividend and income index products. People own this for the coupon.

The mechanical risk follows directly. A dividend rebase - not a suspension, simply a cut to restore coverage after a year in which the payout exceeded earnings and net debt rose to fund it - would force yield mandates and high-dividend index products to sell, and they would sell without reference to whether EUR 4.00 or EUR 3.70 was a sensible price for the assets. That is the specific washout scenario worth pre-positioning for, and it is the one that would produce the entry level this thesis actually deserves.

A washout of that kind has not happened. The stock is 4% off its twelve-month low, which means it has drifted down rather than flushed - the pattern of holders quietly reducing, not of forced liquidation. Two supporting observations. The insider buy ratio is zero: with the shares at a twelve-month low and a 7.2% yield on offer, no insider stepped in, and that silence from people who can see the contract negotiation is information. The smart-money score of 9 out of 100 and institutional flow at a neutral 50 out of 100 say the same thing differently - nobody informed is accumulating.

One structural point cuts the other way and limits how bad any flush can get. RAI holds about two-thirds of the shares, so the genuine free float is roughly a third of a EUR 1.23 billion company - call it EUR 400 million. A thin float amplifies moves in both directions, and it means a forced-selling episode would overshoot further than the fundamentals justify. That is a reason to want the washout, not to fear it.
moderator_conclusion:
Wait for the wash-out. This is a good asset at an unremarkable price, and the discipline of this book is to buy good assets at remarkable ones.

The business is what it appears to be. Rai Way owns the only national broadcast transmission network in Italy - roughly 2,300 permissioned sites that cannot be rebuilt, carrying signals under a legal universal-coverage mandate. It earns 25.3% on invested capital and 47.0% on equity, generated EUR 141.8 million of operating cash flow in 2025, carries net debt of only 0.90 times cash profit, and has raised revenue every year for eleven years. The forensic file is clean in the sense that matters: nothing here is misstated, the cash is real, the solvency is not in question, and the one guided number available to test - first-quarter core revenue up 2.6% to EUR 71.9 million - was delivered exactly.

The valuation says the same thing twice, which is the most reassuring feature of this analysis. Valuing the parts separately - the core anchor contract at about 8.5 times cash profit, the third-party tower leasing and network services at about 11 times, less EUR 168 million of net debt - gives EUR 5.55 a share. Cross-checking against sustainable free cash flow of roughly EUR 0.39 to EUR 0.41 a share and asking what yield a 0.42-beta contracted infrastructure asset should clear at, given a fair spread over long-dated Italian government debt, gives EUR 5.20 to EUR 5.60. Two independent methods, one answer. Against a live price of EUR 4.57 in Milan, that is a discount in the high teens - real, but not the kind of discount that earns a large position in a tape that is demanding wider entry margins.

Three things hold this back from a purchase today. First, the moat is narrow and its trend is eroding, and I want to be precise about what that means rather than hiding behind the label. The monopoly is physical and genuine, but a monopoly whose only customer is also its controlling shareholder is a cost-plus relationship, not pricing power - and the evidence of erosion is arithmetic, not opinion: operating margin down about 400 basis points in two years, absolute operating profit down about 5% on revenue up about 4%, earnings per share falling for two years running. The mitigating reading, which I believe is the more likely one, is that this is dilution from lower-margin new activity rather than the core being priced down - gross margin is stable while operating margin falls, which points below the gross line to depreciation. But likely is not proven, and the proof arrives on 11 November 2026, not today.

Second, the structural discount to the tower peer group is largely deserved and should not be booked as opportunity. Our peer work flags Rai Way as cheap against Cellnex, INWIT and the American tower landlords, with the caveat that the conclusion holds absent an idiosyncratic overhang. The overhang is the ownership structure, in plain sight. And a meaningful slice of the de-rating is shared with the entire bond-substitute complex - long-dated yields at nineteen-year highs compress every infrastructure multiple simultaneously - which is sector beta, not single-name edge.

Third, and decisively for the timing call: the most natural path from EUR 4.57 to EUR 5.55 runs through a lower discount rate, and that is a bet on falling long yields. In an environment where the long end has refused to rally even as near-term tightening was priced out, a thesis that needs rates to rescue it is a thesis this book declines. Strip that mechanism out and the re-rating has to be earned operationally, over eighteen months rather than six.

On the catalyst, I want to be explicit that it is not what is holding the score down. There is a real driver with no fixed date - restoration of the medium-term plan and clarity on the anchor contract - and the 30 July 2026 guidance raise is already spent news that moved nothing. In this book a spent or undated event is neither a credit nor a penalty; what I have scored is the residual value case on its own merits, and that case is sound but not compelling at this price.

The level I am waiting for is specific: EUR 4.10 or below, which is roughly a 26% discount to fair value and pushes the dividend yield past 8%. The most likely route there is a dividend rebase - the payout consumed about 101% of earnings in 2025 and net debt rose EUR 54 million in the quarter it was paid - which would force the income and high-dividend index holders out mechanically against a free float of only about EUR 400 million. That flush would overshoot, and it is the entry this asset deserves. The alternative trigger, which would take me to the same conclusion from the other direction, is the 11 November 2026 report re-affirming the raised guidance and restoring a credible 2027 plan: that would convert the eroding-margin question from unresolved to answered, and would justify paying up rather than waiting down.

Until one of those two arrives, this is a name to hold on the list and not in the book.

# Forensic Dossier — Rai Way S.p.A. (RWAY.MI, Borsa Italiana)

**Date of review:** 31 August 2026 · **Price used:** EUR 4.57 (live quote, Milan) · **Market value:** about EUR 1.23 billion

**A note on sources before anything else.** No earnings-call transcript exists for this company in our licensed data feed, and none could be retrieved from the open web — Rai Way is a mid-cap Italian issuer that publishes results in Italian and does not distribute a transcript through the usual English-language channels. Everything below is therefore built from two things only: the hard quarterly financial statements (revenue, margins, cash flow, balance sheet) pulled from the licensed feed, and a small number of dated news items I was able to confirm. Where I would normally quote management, I say plainly that I cannot. No quotation in this dossier is invented, and no figure is presented as sourced when it is my own estimate.

Rai Way owns and runs the transmission network that carries Italy's public television and radio signals — roughly 2,300 towers and sites, plus the satellite, microwave and fibre links between them. It was carved out of RAI, the state broadcaster, and floated in November 2014. RAI still owns about two-thirds of it and remains, by a wide margin, its largest customer.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Without transcripts I cannot trace how management's language evolved quarter by quarter. What I can trace, from the numbers and the dated public record, is how the *story the market is willing to pay for* has evolved — and that arc is unusually clear.

**Phase one (2021–2024): the quiet compounder.** Revenue climbed from EUR 230 million in 2021 to EUR 276 million in 2024, earnings per share from EUR 0.24 to EUR 0.33, and the dividend rose every year. Operating cash flow ran between EUR 117 million and EUR 147 million a year against a market value that peaked north of EUR 1.7 billion. The story was simple and it was true: a regulated-feeling monopoly asset with a state-backed anchor customer, throwing off cash, gradually adding third-party tenants to towers that were already built and paid for.

**Phase two (2025–2026): the story gets more expensive to tell.** The top line kept grinding higher — EUR 283 million in 2025, and EUR 286.6 million over the twelve months to June 2026 — but the profit stopped following it. Earnings per share have now printed EUR 0.32, EUR 0.33, EUR 0.33 for 2023, 2024 and 2025 and have slipped to EUR 0.314 over the trailing twelve months. The second quarter of 2026 earned EUR 0.0827 a share against EUR 0.092 a year earlier, a decline of about 10%. Depreciation has risen from EUR 47.3 million in 2023 to EUR 56.4 million in 2025, which tells you where the money went: into building things.

**Phase three (late 2025 to now): the market stops paying for the compounder.** The shares have fallen from EUR 6.34 to EUR 4.46 at the low and sit at EUR 4.57 today, roughly 28% below the twelve-month high and about 17% below the 200-day average. Two things are documented. Kepler Cheuvreux cut the stock from Buy to Hold on 9 July 2026, lowering its target from EUR 6.70 to EUR 5.20. Morgan Stanley published an Equalweight rating with a EUR 5.40 target on 26 August 2026. Investing.com attributes the sharpest single leg of the decline to the company resetting its 2027 outlook alongside a third-quarter report — I was **not** able to establish the exact date of that reset from a primary source, so I carry it as reported-but-unconfirmed, and I flag it as the single most important thing a director should verify before committing capital.

The arc, then, is a business whose revenue narrative is intact and whose *earnings* narrative quietly broke, followed by a market that repriced the multiple rather than the sales line.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

I cannot test management's spoken claims. I can test the two claims the company made in public in 2026 — that the first quarter showed "solid" growth, and that the full-year outlook deserved to be raised on 30 July 2026 — against what the statements actually show.

| Claim (dated) | What the financials show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Not assessable from primary evidence.** No transcripts were obtainable, so I have no quotations, no analyst exchanges, and no basis to score whether management's language moved from offensive to defensive. I will not manufacture that assessment.

What I can observe is *behavioural* tone, which is a weaker but real signal. On 30 July 2026 management chose to raise full-year guidance in a half-year in which cash profit and net profit both declined. That is a confident act. Set against it, the reported reset of the 2027 outlook is a retreat from a longer-dated promise. Confident about the next six months, less confident about the next twenty-four, is the shape that emerges — and it is a shape that usually reflects genuine near-term contract visibility sitting on top of genuine medium-term uncertainty, rather than evasion.

**Trajectory rating: not rated on quoted evidence. Behavioural read: stable near-term confidence, reduced medium-term confidence.**

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

There is one clean, dated test available and the company passed it: Q1 2026 core revenue was guided and reported at about 2.6% growth to roughly EUR 72 million, and the statements show exactly EUR 71.9 million, up 2.6%. Rai Way's revenue is largely contracted, so hitting a revenue number is close to arithmetic rather than achievement.

Against that sits the reported reset of the 2027 outlook. Resetting a plan is itself a statement that the earlier plan was not deliverable, and a director should weight it accordingly — the credibility debit belongs to the original plan, not to the reset. Because I could not confirm the date or the magnitude of that reset from a primary source, I hold the debit but do not size it.

The forward consensus is worth stating precisely, because it defines what management now has to deliver: analysts model revenue of EUR 290.3 million and earnings per share of EUR 0.328 for 2026, EUR 303.9 million and EUR 0.344 for 2027, EUR 315.4 million and EUR 0.362 for 2028, reaching EUR 360 million of revenue and EUR 0.406 of earnings per share by 2030. That is a compound revenue growth rate of about 4.4% a year for four years, versus the roughly 2% the company has actually delivered recently. **The street is modelling an acceleration that the trailing numbers do not yet show.** That gap is the live credibility question.

**Reliability score: Medium.** Revenue promises are kept because revenue is contracted. Profit promises have not kept pace, and one multi-year plan has been reset.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Without transcripts I cannot list the questions management deflected. I can name the four issues that any competent analyst is pressing on, all of which are visible in the numbers or the ownership structure, and none of which the public record answers:

1. **Customer concentration.** RAI is both the controlling shareholder and the dominant customer. The exact share of revenue is not disclosed in the data available to me, but the company was created as RAI's transmission arm and the relationship governs the business. This is not a diversified tower company with a dozen tenants; it is one contract with a state broadcaster whose own funding — the Italian licence fee — is set by politicians.
2. **What the 2027 reset actually changed.** The single unanswered question in the file.
3. **Where the incremental capital is going, and what it earns.** Depreciation is up about 19% since 2023 while operating profit is down. Something is being built. The returns on it are not yet visible.
4. **Whether the dividend is a promise or a policy.** At about EUR 0.33 a share the payout is roughly 105% of trailing earnings and roughly 84% of trailing free cash flow on the narrower cash-flow definition. It is covered, but it is not comfortably covered, and it is being paid partly by letting net debt drift up.

**Topics analysts worry about that the disclosure does not address:** the terminal demand for digital terrestrial broadcasting, and what the anchor contract looks like when it is next repriced.

---

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 **Operating profit is falling while revenue rises.** EUR 132.2 million (2024) to EUR 130.1 million (2025) to EUR 125.5 million (trailing twelve months to June 2026), against revenue up about 4%. Three margin lines down two years running.

🔴 **Guidance was raised on 30 July 2026 into a half-year where cash profit fell 0.9% and net profit fell 6.7%.** Not disqualifying, but it demands an explanation the public record does not supply.

🔴 **Earnings per share are going backwards.** EUR 0.33 for 2024 and 2025, EUR 0.314 trailing, and the June 2026 quarter down about 10% year on year.

🔴 **A multi-year plan was reset** (reported, date unconfirmed) — and the shares have not recovered since.

🔴 **The dividend now moves the balance sheet.** Net debt rose EUR 54 million in the quarter the dividend was paid; shareholders' equity fell from EUR 213.8 million to EUR 147.5 million over the same three months.

🔴 **Single-customer, single-country, and the customer is the controlling shareholder.** Any repricing of the anchor contract is negotiated with a counterparty that also controls the board.

🟢 **The cash generation is real and it is large.** Operating cash flow of EUR 141.8 million in 2025 on a business valued at EUR 1.23 billion. Free cash flow yield of roughly 10% on the narrower capital-expenditure definition, roughly 8.6% if you charge the full property and equipment spend.

🟢 **Returns remain exceptional in absolute terms.** 25.3% on invested capital, 47.0% on equity, 64.9% cash-profit margins. Even after two years of erosion these are numbers most listed companies never reach.

🟢 **The balance sheet is not the problem.** Net debt of EUR 168 million including EUR 26.7 million of capitalised leases (about EUR 141 million excluding them) is 0.90 times cash profit. Solvency score of 3.9 on the Altman scale is comfortably out of the danger zone.

🟢 **Revenue has never declined.** Eleven straight years of dividends, and a top line that has risen every year through a pandemic, an energy shock and an inflation cycle.

🟢 **Q1 2026 was delivered exactly as advertised** (+2.6% to EUR 71.9 million), and the guidance raise on 30 July 2026, whatever its tension with the profit line, is a public commitment management now has to meet at the 11 November 2026 print.

---

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

**The depreciation line is the tell.** It rose from EUR 47.3 million in 2023 to EUR 56.4 million in 2025 while cash profit stayed flat. Depreciation is the delayed cost of yesterday's building. A company whose depreciation is compounding faster than its cash profit is a company whose asset base is growing faster than the earnings that base produces. That is either the early phase of a good investment or the middle phase of a bad one, and the accounts alone cannot tell you which.

**The margin mix is diluting, not collapsing.** Gross margin is described as stable at 56.7% while the operating margin fell about 400 basis points in two years. Stable gross margin with falling operating margin means the pressure is below the gross line — depreciation and overhead — not in pricing. Read literally, that says the legacy transmission contract is *not* being priced down; the new, lower-margin activities the company describes in its own profile (leasing tower space to third parties, network management, multimedia and value-added services) are simply diluting a spectacular average. That is an important distinction: dilution from growth is a very different animal from erosion from competition.

**The share count moves, slightly.** Weighted shares run between roughly 268.4 million and 272.1 million across recent quarters, with EUR 19.3 million of treasury stock on the balance sheet. Small, but it means per-share arithmetic should use the roughly 268.5 million shares outstanding net of treasury, not the 272 million issued.

**Nobody is buying.** The insider buy ratio in the screen is zero and the smart-money score is 9 out of 100. At a twelve-month low, with a 7.2% dividend yield, no insider stepped in. That silence is information.

---

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: STABLE.** Not strengthening — operating profit and earnings per share have gone backwards two years running. Not deteriorating — revenue has never fallen, cash profit is essentially flat rather than declining, the balance sheet is sound, and the dividend is covered. This is a high-quality asset in a mild, self-inflicted, investment-driven earnings trough, not a business losing its market.

**The single most important thing to weigh before sizing:** *the anchor contract with RAI is simultaneously the entire moat and the entire risk, and it is negotiated with the company's own controlling shareholder.* Everything else on this page — the 7.2% yield, the 25% returns, the eleven-year dividend record — is downstream of one commercial relationship with a state broadcaster funded by a licence fee that Italian politics keeps revisiting. You are not underwriting a diversified infrastructure portfolio. You are underwriting one contract, held by a counterparty who sits on both sides of the table. Size for that, not for the 0.42 beta.

**Moat type: regulatory-license plus scale-cost.** Rai Way owns the only national broadcast transmission network in Italy. It cannot be rebuilt economically, its sites carry planning and emissions permits that are effectively unobtainable today, and the national coverage obligation that funds it is a public-service mandate. That is a genuine, physical, permissioned moat.

**Moat width: NARROW, and the trend is ERODING.** Narrow rather than wide because a monopoly with one customer who also owns you is not a pricing moat — it is a cost-plus relationship, and the returns it produces are whatever the counterparty allows. Eroding rather than stable because the evidence says so on the standard we apply: operating margin down about 400 basis points in two years, absolute operating profit down about 5% on revenue up about 4%, earnings per share falling, and invested capital rising. I want to be precise about *why* it is eroding, because it changes what a buyer is underwriting: the erosion appears to come from mix — lower-margin new activities diluting a 65% cash-profit core — rather than from the core being priced down. That is the better of the two explanations, but it still means the marginal euro of capital is earning far less than the average one.

**Secular threat: MATERIAL, not terminal.** The structural force is the long decline of linear broadcast television as viewing migrates to internet delivery. It is real and it is directional: over a fifteen-to-twenty-year horizon, terrestrial broadcast towers carry less of the country's video. But three things stop it being terminal on any horizon this committee underwrites. Italy has among the highest terrestrial-television penetration in Europe. The public-service universal-coverage obligation is a legal mandate, not a commercial choice, and it does not lapse because viewing habits shift. And the same physical sites are being re-purposed for third-party hosting and network services, which is precisely what the diluting revenue mix represents. Consensus agrees: analysts model revenue rising to EUR 360 million by 2030 from EUR 290 million this year. Nobody is forecasting decline.

**Is the cheapness a fear-print or a value trap?** Neither cleanly, which is the honest answer. It is not a value trap: the base is not shrinking, the cash flow is contracted, leverage is low and the dividend is covered. But it is not a straightforward fear-print either, because the market did not de-rate this stock on panic — it de-rated it on a reset multi-year plan, two analyst downgrades from firms that had been positive, and a nineteen-year high in long-dated government bond yields that mechanically compresses what any 7%-yielding, 0.42-beta infrastructure asset is worth. Those are reasons, not fear. The mispricing, if there is one, is modest and it is in the multiple, not in the earnings power.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.

Leverage is still low, but a dividend that exceeds earnings and is partly funded by borrowing is a dividend with a shelf life if the investment programme continues.

Fifth, the market repriced this for reasons, not out of panic. Kepler Cheuvreux, which had a Buy and a EUR 6.70 target on 11 May 2026, downgraded to Hold with a EUR 5.20 target on 9 July 2026. Morgan Stanley published Equalweight with a EUR 5.40 target on 26 August 2026. Both current targets sit below any bullish reading of fair value. And a 0.42-beta, 7%-yielding infrastructure asset is a bond substitute: with long-dated government yields at nineteen-year highs, the discount rate applied to this cash flow stream has risen mechanically, and no amount of operational delivery fixes that.

What would confirm the bear case: the 11 November 2026 third-quarter report showing the guidance raise walked back or the 2027 outlook cut again; any disclosure that the RAI contract is being renegotiated on worse terms; a fourth consecutive quarter of falling earnings per share; or a dividend rebased to restore coverage. Any one of those would take the shares below EUR 4.00 quickly, because the shareholder register here is full of people who own it for the yield and nothing else.
consensus_delta:
Where we disagree with the market is narrower than the 28% drawdown suggests, and being honest about that is the point of this section.

The street is not pricing terminal decline into this company. That is the first thing to establish, because with a stock 28% off its high and sitting 4% off a twelve-month low, the reflex is to assume the market has written the business off. It has not. Consensus models revenue rising from EUR 290.3 million in 2026 to EUR 303.9 million in 2027, EUR 315.4 million in 2028 and EUR 360 million by 2030, with earnings per share of EUR 0.406 by the end of that path - compound revenue growth of about 4.4% a year. What the market has actually done is compress the multiple while leaving the forecasts alone, and there are two identifiable reasons, one of which we think is right and one of which we think is overdone.

The reason we think is right: the anchor contract is a genuine structural discount, not a temporary fear. RAI owns about two-thirds of the equity and buys the large majority of the output. A minority holder in that structure does not own a monopoly's pricing power; they own whatever a controlling counterparty leaves on the table. The market is correct to demand a permanent discount for that, and any thesis that treats the gap to diversified tower operators as recoverable alpha is mispricing the governance.

The reason we think is overdone: the profit deterioration is being read as erosion when the evidence says dilution. Gross margin is stable at 56.7% while operating margin has fallen about 400 basis points in two years. Stable gross margin with falling operating margin means the pressure sits below the gross line - in depreciation, which rose from EUR 47.3 million in 2023 to EUR 56.4 million in 2025 - and not in pricing. Read literally, the legacy contract is not being priced down; new, lower-margin third-party activity is diluting a spectacular 65% cash-profit average. Growth dilution and competitive erosion look identical on a margin chart and are opposite in what they imply. Both sit below our EUR 5.55 base, and both were set by analysts who had been materially more positive within the last four months. The disagreement worth naming, finally, is about the re-rating mechanism itself - and here we disagree with the bulls, not the bears. The most plausible route to EUR 5.55 for a 0.42-beta asset yielding 7.2% is a lower discount rate. That is a bet on long-dated yields falling, and in the current environment - the long end at nineteen-year highs, the September policy move already priced out without the long end rallying - a rate-rescue thesis is one we deliberately refuse to underwrite. positioning_washout:
This is a yield-owned stock, and that is the most important fact about its shareholder register.

The evidence is circumstantial but consistent. Eleven consecutive years of dividends since the November 2014 flotation. A current payout of about EUR 0.33 a share yielding roughly 7.2%. A beta of 0.42, which is what you get when the holders are income and low-volatility mandates rather than growth money. RAI holds about two-thirds of the shares, so the genuine free float is roughly a third of a EUR 1.23 billion company - call it EUR 400 million. A thin float amplifies moves in both directions, and it means a forced-selling episode would overshoot further than the fundamentals justify. That is a reason to want the washout, not to fear it.
moderator_conclusion:
Wait for the wash-out. This is a good asset at an unremarkable price, and the discipline of this book is to buy good assets at remarkable ones.

The business is what it appears to be. Rai Way owns the only national broadcast transmission network in Italy - roughly 2,300 permissioned sites that cannot be rebuilt, carrying signals under a legal universal-coverage mandate. It earns 25.3% on invested capital and 47.0% on equity, generated EUR 141.8 million of operating cash flow in 2025, carries net debt of only 0.90 times cash profit, and has raised revenue every year for eleven years. The forensic file is clean in the sense that matters: nothing here is misstated, the cash is real, the solvency is not in question, and the one guided number available to test - first-quarter core revenue up 2.6% to EUR 71.9 million - was delivered exactly.

The valuation says the same thing twice, which is the most reassuring feature of this analysis. Valuing the parts separately - the core anchor contract at about 8.5 times cash profit, the third-party tower leasing and network services at about 11 times, less EUR 168 million of net debt - gives EUR 5.55 a share. Cross-checking against sustainable free cash flow of roughly EUR 0.39 to EUR 0.41 a share and asking what yield a 0.42-beta contracted infrastructure asset should clear at, given a fair spread over long-dated Italian government debt, gives EUR 5.20 to EUR 5.60. Two independent methods, one answer. bull_thesis:
Rai Way owns the physical network that carries Italy's public television and radio signals - roughly 2,300 towers and transmission sites plus the satellite, microwave and fibre links between them. That is a genuine, permissioned, physical moat, and it shows up in the returns: 25.3% on invested capital and 47.0% on equity over the twelve months to June 2026, with cash profit margins of 64.9%. Most listed companies never touch those numbers.

The bull case is that the market has repriced the multiple on this asset without the earnings power having changed. The shares trade at EUR 4.57 in Milan against a twelve-month high of EUR 6.34 - down about 28% - and sit roughly 17% below their 200-day average, only 4% up off the low. The reason we think is right: the anchor contract is a genuine structural discount, not a temporary fear. RAI owns about two-thirds of the equity and buys the large majority of the output. A minority holder in that structure does not own a monopoly's pricing power; they own whatever a controlling counterparty leaves on the table. The market is correct to demand a permanent discount for that, and any thesis that treats the gap to diversified tower operators as recoverable alpha is mispricing the governance.

The reason we think is overdone: the profit deterioration is being read as erosion when the evidence says dilution. Stable gross margin with falling operating margin means the pressure sits below the gross line - in depreciation, which rose from EUR 47.3 million in 2023 to EUR 56.4 million in 2025 - and not in pricing. Read literally, the legacy contract is not being priced down; new, lower-margin third-party activity is diluting a spectacular 65% cash-profit average. Growth dilution and competitive erosion look identical on a margin chart and are opposite in what they imply. Both sit below our EUR 5.55 base, and both were set by analysts who had been materially more positive within the last four months. That looks like targets marked to a falling price rather than to a changed forecast, which is the most common form of sell-side drift. But we are talking about a EUR 0.15 to EUR 0.35 disagreement on a EUR 4.57 stock. That is a difference of view, not an expectations arbitrage.

# Rai Way S.p.A. (RWAY.MI, Milan, EUR) - a deep dive on management and the setup

As of 29 September 2026. Live price EUR 4.335 on Borsa Italiana (FMP quote; day range EUR 4.32-4.37, a new twelve-month low of EUR 4.32 against a high of EUR 6.25; 50-day average EUR 4.57, 200-day average EUR 5.39). No earnings-call transcript is available from FMP for this listing. Sources used: the Q1 2026 call summary published by Investing.com (May 2026), Il Sole 24 Ore / Radiocor coverage of the 30 July 2026 half-year call, MarketScreener (1 July 2026) on the collapse of the EI Towers merger talks, Websim (6 July 2026) on RAI weighing a sale of 10% of Rai Way, and the screener's financial trajectory. Quotes are limited to phrases those sources carry; nothing below is invented.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

For roughly eighteen months (late 2024 to June 2026) the Rai Way story was a consolidation story. The controlling shareholder RAI (the Italian state broadcaster, about 65% owner), the infrastructure fund F2i and MediaForEurope had a memorandum of understanding to merge Rai Way with EI Towers, the rival broadcast-tower operator, creating a national operator with about 4,700 sites and more than EUR 500 million of revenue. Management's language in that period was about waiting: in March 2026 the CEO, Roberto Cecatto, said the memorandum was days from expiry and "we are waiting for an update"; in the Q1 2026 call (May) he asked for "a stability environment for the company" while the shareholders negotiated governance.

That memorandum expired on 30 June 2026 without agreement (MarketScreener, 1 July 2026), reportedly over the exchange ratio, debt, governance and service contracts. From the 30 July 2026 half-year call onward the narrative contracted to a standalone plan: "since it was not possible to proceed with consolidation, our plan remains valid" (Cecatto, 30 July 2026). The growth drivers now named are the 2024-2027 industrial plan's roughly EUR 240 million of development investment, about EUR 120 million of it earmarked for a start-up network of edge and hyperscale data centres, plus the build-out of digital radio (DAB) and solar self-generation. The takeover premium that a merger implied has been quietly removed from the story, and the data-centre leg has been promoted to the lead growth theme.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Source | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Core revenue grows ahead of inflation | Q1 2026: EUR 72 million, +2.6% vs ~1% inflation | Revenue EUR 230m (2021) to EUR 283m (2025), +2.4% in 2025, 3-yr CAGR +4.8%; never down in any year | Matches |
| Adjusted operating cash profit (EBITDA) "broadly in line with the previous year" | Full-year guidance, confirmed May and July 2026 | Q1 EBITDA EUR 47.3m, +1%; but net income flat EUR 87-90m for three years and latest-quarter earnings per share down about 10% year on year; trailing EPS EUR 0.32 vs 0.33 | Matches on cash profit, but the profit lines below it are slipping |
| Strong cash generation | Q1 FCF EUR 34m, +6.3% | Trailing free cash flow EUR 124m (screener) is a peak window; the three-year average after full investment is nearer EUR 88m (as-reported cash-flow statements, per our prior record) | Headline flattering; the durable figure is lower |
| Deleveraging | Q1 net debt EUR 113.5m, down EUR 23m | Net debt rebounded to EUR 168m at 30 June 2026 (EUR 157m borrowings + EUR 27m leases - EUR 15m cash) after the dividend; the pattern is seasonal, not a trend | Accurate for the quarter quoted; not a structural improvement |
| Growth from digital infrastructure | Q1 digital infrastructure revenue EUR 8.8m, +5.3% | That leg is only ~12% of core revenue; media distribution (the RAI contract) is EUR 63.2m of EUR 72m | Real growth, on too small a base to move the total yet |

The narrative is honest on revenue and cash profit. It is richer than the numbers on growth: the data-centre plan consumes capital now (development capital spending guided above 2025) while earnings per share have gone nowhere for three years.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable, shading defensive. Q1 2026: confident on the core ("the full year guidance provided in March remained valid") but passive on strategy, deferring to shareholders. 30 July 2026: conciliatory on the failed deal ("we accept this outcome as a given fact") and firm on the plan. Guidance has become less ambitious, not more: the target is cash profit held level with 2025 at constant electricity prices, with about EUR 3 million of underlying growth offset by non-core items. There is no language of acceleration.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Reliability: High on what is guided, which is narrow. The Q1 2026 core-revenue and cash-profit prints landed on the guided trajectory; the full-year outlook was confirmed in both May and July 2026. Management guides a small number of flat-ish metrics and delivers them. The medium-term industrial plan targets (to 2027) are the untested part, and the prior committee file recorded that the market read the 2027 outlook as reset downward; I could not confirm from a primary source exactly what changed. The next test is the third-quarter report scheduled for 11 November 2026.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- Credit lines and the master service agreement with RAI (Intermonte, Q1 2026): whether the anchor contract with the controlling shareholder is up for revision. Management did not give terms. This is the single most important undisclosed variable.
- Data-centre timing and customers (Mediobanca, Q1 2026): analysts want evidence of hyperscale demand before the capital goes in. No named customers were disclosed in the sources reviewed.
- Consolidation: asked repeatedly through 2025-26; the answer was always that it was a shareholder matter, and it ended in no deal.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flag (30 June 2026): the EI Towers merger - the market's expected exit - expired without agreement; the takeover optionality that supported the multiple is gone.
Red flag (6 July 2026, Websim): RAI is reported to be weighing a sale of about 10% of Rai Way; a placement into weak demand would likely clear at a discount, an overhang on the share price.
Red flag (Q2 2026): latest-quarter earnings per share down about 10% year on year; net and operating margins have compressed for two years while revenue rose.
Red flag (2025): dividends of about EUR 90 million consumed roughly all of reported net profit; net debt rises each spring to fund the payout.
Green flag (every year since 2014 flotation): revenue has never declined; the transmission network is irreplaceable and legally mandated.
Green flag (Q1 2026): underlying external cost growth held to 2.4% (CFO Adalberto Pellegrino), solid cost discipline.
Green flag: net debt around 0.9 times cash profit, Altman-Z 3.8 - solvency is not a question.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The vocabulary moved from "consolidation" and "aggregation" to "integrated digital infrastructure operator" and "edge and hyperscale data centres" - a company rewriting its equity story after losing its exit. The capital-allocation mix is shifting from pure payout toward growth capital spending at the same time as earnings are flat, which raises the question of whether the dividend (about EUR 0.33 a share, roughly 7.6% at today's price) can keep growing. No management change; the CEO and CFO are unchanged. Insider buying is nil at a twelve-month low.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: STABLE. Revenue compounds slowly, cash profit is flat by guidance, and the business is solvent and cash-generative; nothing is deteriorating fast, but nothing is improving either.

The single most important thing to weigh: the minority owns a cost-plus contract with its own controlling shareholder. The value of this equity depends on the terms of the RAI service agreement, which no outsider can see or date - and RAI may now also be a seller of shares.

Moat: regulatory-license / physical-network. The roughly 2,300 permissioned sites cannot be rebuilt, and returns remain high (return on invested capital 23.8%, return on equity 44%). But the width is narrow rather than wide, because the pricing power belongs to the counterparty (RAI), not to Rai Way, and operating margins have drifted down for two years (the prior committee file tracked operating margin at 47.9%, 45.7%, 43.8%). Moat trend: eroding at the margin, not collapsing.

Secular threat: material, not terminal. Linear broadcast television is in slow structural decline as viewing moves to streaming over broadband, which over a decade reduces the value of terrestrial transmission; but the universal-coverage public-service mandate and radio/DAB keep the network necessary for the foreseeable future, and contracted revenue has kept rising. The cheapness is partly a fear-print (loss of merger optionality, rate-driven de-rating of bond substitutes) and partly a correctly priced structural discount for a captive, slowly shrinking end-market.
